headline: High risk: Cline’s broad workspace write/network/MCP capabilities can conflict with Botpress’s agentic outputs, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is an agentic chatbot that can emit instruction-like content, while Cline can use MCP, read/write workspace files, and run browsers. A shared file or MCP bridge could let Botpress outputs be treated as instructions by Cline. The pairwise pathway is plausible from profiles alone, but not directly documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Botpress output is copied into a workspace file or MCP payload that Cline reads as instructions, injection is possible.
IF Cline is configured to ingest Botpress-generated text without provenance checks, prompt hijacking risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Botpress outputs into Cline tools.
Add provenance tags to Botpress-generated content before any handoff.
Restrict Cline MCP servers to allowlisted, read-only endpoints.
Use a separate workspace directory for Botpress artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has no network egress, but Cline has broad network egress, reads workspace files, and handles model-provider API keys. If Botpress touches sensitive support data and that data lands in Cline’s workspace, Cline can transmit it outward. The profiles show a realistic shared-workspace leakage path, though Botpress’s touched data classes are empty, so I keep this at medium.
conditions: IF sensitive support transcripts are written into the shared workspace, Cline can read them.
IF Cline sends workspace contents to its configured model provider or MCP server, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep Botpress artifacts out of Cline’s workspace.
Disable or narrow Cline network egress for shared projects.
Store secrets and transcripts in separate, access-controlled directories.
Review MCP server permissions before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and Cline can execute shells, modify git state, write files, and install packages in the same workspace model. That creates a direct write/write conflict with irreversible repo changes and no locking mechanism shown in either profile. Because Cline’s default workspace sharing is explicit and Botpress has no isolation fields, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can race.
IF Botpress installs or changes packages while Cline edits or commits, git and dependency state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
Require manual review before git commits.
Lock dependency-manifest edits to one agent at a time.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate agentic outputs, and Cline can act on workspace state, run shells, and modify git. If Cline treats Botpress output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes, commits, or browser actions. The default tool-rich execution path makes this dangerous without explicit verification, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Cline uses Botpress output as a task plan without verification, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF Botpress produces malformed code or instructions and Cline executes them, downstream changes may be committed.
mitigations: Require human review of Botpress outputs before Cline acts.
Add a verification step for code, commands, and citations.
Limit Cline to read-only mode for Botpress-generated tasks.
Separate planning from execution across the two agents.
requires-engineering: implement structured handoff schemas with validation.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source. The only concrete compliance-relevant detail is Cline’s handling of model-provider API keys and broad egress; Botpress’s profile does not show a conflicting compliance regime. This is a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Cline and sent to a non-approved model provider, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF Botpress is deployed under a stricter retention policy than Cline’s workspace, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared tasks.
Confirm provider and retention settings before use.
Document data-handling responsibilities for each agent.
Keep audit logs of handoffs and exports.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the deployment.
